title: Bayesian Recursive Self-Improvement
content: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires an agent not only to acquire new knowledge and capabilities, but also to reason about which existing capabilities remain valid, when they should be routed, tested, retained, deprecated, restructured, or replaced, and whether the mechanisms governing these decisions should themselves be modified. We formulate this process as Bayesian Recursive Capability Evolution (BRCE), which separates an observable meta-configuration, comprising the agent's capability archive and improvement-controller configuration, from a latent self-world state representing environmental regime, context-dependent capability validity and competence, and uncertain improvement effectiveness. A controlled state-space model and Bayesian posterior over this self-world state couple the evolution of the external environment with that of the agent's internal capability state, providing a common information basis for contextual routing, retention, active experimentation, structural capability evolution, and recursive self-modification. This formulation treats contradictory evidence not automatically as a reason to overwrite previous knowledge, but as potential evidence for regime change, capability degradation, or missing latent structure. Posterior uncertainty consequently acts as a signal of potential plasticity: strongly supported capabilities can be protected from unnecessary modification, confidently invalid capabilities can be routed away or deprecated without immediate deletion, and uncertain capabilities can motivate informative experiments when useful evidence is available. To translate these beliefs into principled decisions, we develop a mutual-information measure of capability contextuality, expected-information-gain criteria for active self-evaluation, cost-sensitive structural comparison based on Bayes factors, and long-horizon belief-space control over the posterior and meta-configuration. We show that contextuality has a direct predictive interpretation under logarithmic loss, expected information gain is conditional mutual information, cost-free retention can preserve future option value, and the Bayes-optimal self-modification rule weakly dominates an explicit no-modification baseline in posterior expected net value under the assumed model. Finally, we define self-improvement efficiency and Bayesian self-improvement equilibria, distinguishing improvement of capabilities from improvement of the process that produces them. The recursive step arises when the same Bayesian inference-and-decision process is extended to the mechanisms governing future capability evolution themselves. BRCE thereby formulates recursive self-improvement as Bayesian inference and decision-making over an evolving capability space.
